text: The incoherent type-1 feed-forward loop (I1-FFL) -- where X activates both Y and Z, but Y represses Z -- is best characterized as a:
choices: Sign-sensitive delay element that filters out short pulses of X and only responds to sustained input
Pulse generator that produces transient expression of Z and detects fold-change in X rather than its absolute level
Bistable switch that requires cooperative positive feedback to maintain two stable states
Ring oscillator requiring three sequential repressive interactions and a time delay
explanation: In the I1-FFL, X's direct activation of Z is rapid, while the indirect repression through Y builds up more slowly, so Z rises transiently and then falls even though X persists -- a pulse generator that responds to the fold-change in X rather than its steady level. Choice 0 describes the coherent type-1 FFL, its topological opposite. Choice 2 describes a positive-feedback bistable switch, and choice 3 describes a repressilator-style ring oscillator, both entirely different network topologies from a three-node feed-forward loop.
